official.deadline_note: Three published deadlines for the 2027-2028 cycle, each applying to the CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC together: Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match applicants - 1 November 2026; Regular Decision - 1 February 2027; Transfer applicants - 1 March 2027. Late applications are accepted with no penalty or reduction in aid, only a delayed decision.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 school year (published instructions: 'The instructions below are for the 2027-2028 school year')
official.status_note: The Griffin Financial Aid Office is currently publishing instructions and deadlines for the 2027-2028 school year; aid estimates are released mid-December for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match applicants, with financial aid decisions around 1 April for Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision applicants.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: families with income of $100,000 or below with typical assets attend Free - 'Financial aid covers all billed expenses, including tuition, fees, food, housing, and more'; families with income up to $200,000 receive 'Free Tuition Plus' - 'Financial aid covers the full cost of tuition, plus' aid toward fees, food and housing based on individual circumstances.
official.funding_period: per academic year; equals 100% of demonstrated need
benefits: Scholarship funds are grant-based and never need to be repaid, and are designed to cover 100% of demonstrated financial need.

For families with income at or below $100,000 with typical assets: a $2,000 start-up grant (first year), health insurance covered if needed, travel costs between campus and home covered, winter gear, event fees and other activities covered, plus a $2,000 launch grant (junior year) to prepare for post-Harvard life.
A travel allowance is included in the financial aid award of every student on aid to help cover travel to and from Cambridge.
Loans are never required: 'Our aid packages are designed to cover your financial need without additional borrowing' and most students graduate debt-free.
55% of students receive need-based Harvard scholarships; one in four Harvard College families pays nothing to attend.
eligibility: The aid application process is essentially the same for all prospective students, regardless of citizenship or country of residence.
International students are eligible for exactly the same amount of aid as U.S. students; need-blind admissions apply to all applicants including internationals.
Aid is 100% need-based - there are no merit-based awards and Harvard meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students who apply.
There are no quotas or limits of any kind based on citizenship or school location at any point in the admissions process.
Aid decisions are made without regard to whether an applicant has applied for financial assistance.
requirements: CSS Profile filed online via the College Board with Harvard listed as a recipient using code 3434.
IDOC packet submitted through the College Board IDOC Service (opens only after the CSS Profile is completed).
FAFSA (Harvard code E00468) required for U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and other eligible non-citizens.

Common Application with required supplements for admission; SAT or ACT required to meet the standardized testing requirement (exceptional cases: AP, IB, GCSE/A-Level, or national leaving exam results).

English proficiency exam is not required for first-year or transfer applicants, though TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores may be submitted optionally; these cannot be used to meet the testing requirement.
documents: Parents' 2025 income tax document for both parents - in the U.S. the signed 1040 with all pages and schedules including W-2 forms; for many international students, whatever documentation of income and taxes is submitted to their national government.
Student's 2025 income tax document, or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus any W-2 forms received.
Business/Farm Supplement form plus the 2025 business tax return (e.g. 1065, 1120S, 1120 with K-1 statements) for each parental business or farm interest.
Full trust tax return plus a letter explaining the contents, value and accessibility of any estate or trust benefiting the student or parents.

English translations of all non-English documents; self-translation is acceptable for tax documents, while translated school credentials should name the translator and their relationship to the applicant.
Wage statement, pay slip, salary certificate or employer letter stating annual income if a parent does not file a tax return.
selection_criteria: Aid is determined solely by demonstrated need, reviewing family income, assets, expenses, size and unusual financial circumstances.
Expected parent contribution is zero for families with annual incomes below $100,000; families with incomes up to $200,000 have at least full tuition covered by aid.
Every student has a standard expected contribution from earnings, plus a small portion of any savings or assets, usually met through term-time employment.
Families with significant assets are asked to pay more, but home equity and retirement assets are typically not considered.
coverage: All billed expenses - tuition, fees, food and housing - for families with income at or below $100,000 with typical assets (2026-2027 billed subtotal $91,634; total billed and unbilled costs $95,134-$100,134).
Full tuition plus additional need-based aid toward fees, food and housing for families with income up to $200,000.
Travel allowance for travel to and from Cambridge for all students on aid; health insurance ($4,954 for 2026-2027) covered if needed.
$2,000 start-up grant in the first year and $2,000 launch grant in the junior year for qualifying low-income families.
Students are expected to cover $3,500 in personal expenses per academic year, usually through work-study hours.
application_method: Submit the Common Application with required supplements, indicating intention to apply for aid.
File the online CSS Profile via the College Board and include Harvard using code 3434 (one profile for married/cohabiting parents, separate profiles for separated or divorced parents).
Upload all documents through the College Board IDOC Service; the IDOC list is not definitive - use Harvard's published document list and upload extras as 'institution specific required documents'.
File the 2027-2028 FAFSA (code E00468) if a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or other eligible non-citizen.
official.application_route: Apply for admission through the Common Application, then file the CSS Profile (Harvard code 3434), complete the IDOC packet via College Board, and add the FAFSA if a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or eligible non-citizen.
official.citizenship_residency: Identical admissions and financial aid process for all applicants regardless of nationality or citizenship; admissions are need-blind for everyone, including foreign citizens.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - foreign students receive financial aid on exactly the same basis as American students and are eligible for the same amount of aid; foreign students are not eligible for federal funding but have access to the College's own job and scholarship money.
official.duration: Four-year undergraduate program; aid is awarded per academic year and must be reapplied annually
official.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students to campus regardless of their ability to pay, following need-blind admissions and a promise to meet 100% of every admitted student's demonstrated financial need.
official.region: North America - Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States
official.program_type: Need-based institutional financial aid for Harvard College undergraduates (grant scholarship, student employment, optional loans)
official.english_requirement: No English proficiency exam is required for first-year or transfer applicants - TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo scores may be submitted optionally, but cannot be used to meet the standardized testing requirement.

applicant_utility.summary: Harvard College meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students on a strictly need-based basis, and international applicants compete in the same pool with the same aid as Americans, so family finances never affect admission. Your real task is documentary: a CSS Profile plus an IDOC packet with complete 2025 parent tax documents, filed by 1 November 2026 for Restrictive Early Action or 1 February 2027 for Regular Decision. Families earning under $100,000 with typical assets pay nothing at all, while students are still expected to cover about $3,500 a year in personal expenses, normally through a 10-12 hour per week campus job. Run the Net Price Calculator early - your actual package will look very different from the sticker cost of attendance of roughly $95,000-$100,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving applicants from any country whose families cannot afford full cost and who have complete, translatable 2025 tax records.
application_readiness_checklist: Collect both parents' complete filed 2025 tax returns - every page and schedule, not just the summary - plus W-2 forms, before the Portal round opens.
Sit the SAT or ACT well before the deadline and self-report scores; if access is impossible, document why and gather AP, IB, GCSE/A-Level or national leaving exam results instead.
File the CSS Profile (Harvard code 3434) first - IDOC stays locked until it is done - then upload every document the page lists, not just the basic ones IDOC suggests.
Non-English documents: write the translation directly on the document (no certified translation needed) and keep originals with translated versions for school records.
Use the Net Price Calculator with current numbers, then email faoweb@fas.harvard.edu with anything unusual - job loss, medical bills, a business interest - before you are admitted.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting partial tax returns - U.S. families that send only the 1040 main pages without Schedule 1/A/B or W-2s get flagged and delayed.
Assuming IDOC's checklist is complete - Harvard states its own list on the instructions page is the definitive one; missing business/farm or trust documents stall review.
Nicknames or misspelled legal names across the CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC, or a wrong SSN on U.S. submissions, causing mismatched records.
Missing that both separated or divorced parents each file a separate CSS Profile, so half the financial picture never arrives.
Filing late and then expecting a decision alongside admission - aid still comes at full value, but the decision is pushed back, which wrecks deposit planning.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Students are expected to contribute about $3,500 per year in personal expenses, usually earned through term-time work of roughly 10-12 hours per week; parent contribution varies by income and assets (the average is about $13,000-$14,000), and families who wish to borrow can use the Harvard Loan (up to $3,500 per year at 4.0%, no fees) or parent loans, but borrowing is never required.
document_audit: Actual filed 2025 returns only - estimated or draft tax documents are explicitly not accepted, so wait for the filed version if filing is late.
Business or farm interest means a Business/Farm Supplement per entity plus the full 2025 return (1065/1120S/1120 with K-1s) - the most commonly missed international-family item.
Trust or estate beneficiaries need the full trust return plus an explanatory letter covering contents, value and accessibility.
Non-filing parents need a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus employer wage statements or salary certificates; Canadian families file the T-1 General (and T-2 for businesses).
Documents cannot be sent by email - everything goes through the IDOC upload system only.
alerts: The Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match aid deadline (1 November 2026) is only weeks after this verification date - if you are an REA applicant, the CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC all have to be done by then to get a mid-December aid estimate.
Aid materials are not tracked until after the admissions decision, so nothing tells you they are missing in the meantime - keep proof of every submission.

International applicants are typically not eligible for SAT/ACT fee waivers and may be shut out of the CSS Profile's built-in waiver; Harvard publishes an alternate application route for those who cannot pay or live where College Board cannot process payment.
Applying for aid is need-blind, but the aid application still has to be filed at all - checking nothing means no package is built for you.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Common Application for admission, then CSS Profile to IDOC document upload (FAFSA for U.S. persons), with the aid decision arriving with the admissions decision or shortly after admission once documents are verified.
